analyst_view.overall: Girona (4th) and Eibar (5th) are level on 24 points, so this is a direct fight for the play-off places; Eibar are five games without a win but have been creating plenty, while Girona have taken only 10 of their points at home. Quique Álvarez's Girona get Vanat and Asprilla back from international duty but are short at the back: Àlex Moreno is banned and Furtado, Bryan Gil and Jastin García are injured (all in the numbers), and Javi Boñar (injured) and Holmes Junior (with Spain Under-18) are also missing, which is not in the numbers and may mean Abdul Mumin starting at left-back. Jokin Aranbarri's Eibar have almost a full squad, with only Gift, Imanol and Bernat still in the gym, and Arbilla is one yellow away from a ban. The referee is Alejandro Morilla of the Navarre committee, who is not yet in the numbers and has shown few cards in the Segunda games we have on record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already add for Àlex Moreno's absence from Girona's defence and take a little off for Bryan Gil and Jastin García. I lean slightly higher to about 2.3 because Girona are also without Boñar and Holmes Junior and are expected to use Mumin, a centre-back, at left-back, against an Eibar side that Aranbarri wants to be vertical and quick on the break.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, already lifted for Eibar conceding 44 corners in their last six. Aranbarri plans to sit compact and defend his box when Girona have the ball, which fits a home-heavy corner split the numbers already show (5.9 to 3.5), so nothing new moves it and I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards and were made before the referee was named, so they do not count him. Alejandro Morilla averaged under 4 cards in the seven Segunda games we have on record with him, a small sample, so I trim it to about 5.1; the play-off stakes and Arbilla playing on four yellows keep the cut modest.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting (Eibar 91 in their last six). Girona's patched defence could give Eibar a little more, but Girona's attack is whole again with Vanat back and Carles Pérez and Abel Ruiz expected to start, so I stay at 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target and already count Eibar's accurate recent shooting (35 on target in six). With Girona missing Boñar and Holmes Junior on top of the ban the numbers count, and a centre-back likely at left-back, Eibar's direct attacks should find a little more, so I nudge it to about 9.4.
